messages:
elaine: Quick clarifying question from today's all-hands about credits/quota behavior when customers change plans. TL;DR: what persists vs what resets? :question:

matt: High level: quotas & rate limits are tied to the active plan. Credits (promos, one-offs) are account-level state and persist until consumed or expired. But there are subtle cases.

sophia: More detail: upgrade -> new quotas apply immediately for new allocation. Any outstanding promo credits remain at their original value. We don't auto-top-up promo credits to match higher tiers.

elaine: If we applied an outage buffer (temporary extra tokens) and the customer moves to Dedicated, does that buffer follow?
matt: Yes. Outage buffers are tagged to account_id and live independently of plan. They expire at the buffer TTL. We store them as metadata on the billing bucket.

sam: Finance: consumed credits are never clawed back on downgrade. Unused committed credits may be refunded case-by-case; escalate via billing support.

riley: Rate limits: we have separate soft SLOs for requests/sec and token quotas. Provisioning for upgraded rate limits runs through the pipeline and usually takes <5 minutes; until then the previous rate limit is enforced.

elaine: About fallback routing (fallthrough) to cheaper variants: does that bill at the fallback model rate?
sophia: Yes. Billing is applied at the model variant actually served. We record model_id in traces and in the billing breakdown so customers can see it.

andre: Customer-safety note: when fallthrough changes price by >10% we emit an event and an account-level billing note. Customers can opt in/out for auto-fallbacks in account settings.

elaine: Streaming: if a stream is cut mid-response due to rate limiting, what tokens get billed?
riley: Tokens are metered at flush/commit boundaries (chunk flush or end-of-message). If cut mid-stream, tokens up to the last confirmed flush are billed. We include headers like X-Stream-Flushed-Tokens and X-RateLimit-Remaining. Example:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 14
X-Stream-Flushed-Tokens: 1320
```

sam: Partial-stream billing is deducted from credits; only manual or post-facto adjustments can refund.

elaine: For launch-day spikes: what's the temporary quota increase path?
sophia: Self-serve temporary quota requests in Console (beta next month). Until then use support with "quota-increase" tag and include expected RPS and duration. Example payload for support API:

```
POST /v1/admin/quota-requests
{
  "account_id": "acct_ABC",
  "reason": "launch",
  "start_ts": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-05-03T00:00:00Z",
  "tokens_per_min": 400000,
  "contact": "eng@example.com"
}
```

matt: Ops SLA: forms with telemetry usually approved within 24h; multi-region requests allow 48h.

elaine: Do our internal health checks count against customer quotas? Customers worried probes will use credits.
riley: Managed health-checks from our probe IPs and agent API keys are excluded. Customer-originated pings count. Recommend customers use our low-cost health endpoint for frequent checks.

andre: For synthetic load/testing, we can provision an isolated testing bucket so tests don't touch prod credits. Contact support to provision.

elaine: Any public roadmap dates to call out?
sophia: Roadmap snippets: self-serve quota UI: mid-May. Route-level billing visibility (beta): June. Automated fallthrough alerts for >10% price delta: rolling April. Docs + console banners before rollouts.

matt: We'll add an FAQ link in the all-hands follow-up and schedule customer-scenario syncs on request.

billing-bot: Note created: BILL-534 - add Console help copy + fallthrough event triggers.

elaine: Thanks everyone, saving this thread for the all-hands notes.
sam: Filing follow-up for refund-edge-cases with finance.
andre: I'll draft the support playbook for downgrade/refund handling.
matt: Great, end thread.
